top_stories.ai_overview: Searching for distant planets with Astra Two amateur astronomers used Codex and Astra to look for signs of planets in public telescope data. Now they’ve given professional astronomers a few places to look more closely.
top_stories.ai_what_happened: Astronomers have confirmed more than 6,400 planets beyond our solar system(opens in a new window) since the first ones were announced in 1992(opens in a new window).
ai_key_details: A worldwide community of amateur astronomers has long been part of that search.
Some comb through public telescope data for small, repeated dips in a star’s brightness that could signal an orbiting planet.
Working independently of Bond, he tried several AI models before choosing Astra to help him analyze telescope data from about 19 million stars.
The Codex search found a dip in brightness every 13.8 days.

ai_key_takeaways: Others use their own telescopes to watch for the next dip and share what they see with researchers.

top_stories.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
top_stories.one_liner: How perplexity measures progress in AI models, and why it could help developers establish a shared approach to evaluating emerging capabilities.
top_stories.summary: How perplexity measures progress in AI models, and why it could help developers establish a shared approach to evaluating emerging capabilities.
top_stories.ai_overview: From afar, it might seem like modern AI is built similarly to how software has been built in previous decades: with a diverse set of techniques targeting specific capabilities. There are indeed a variety of methods, but rather than designing something from scratch, they are mostly harnessing the intelligence coming from a much simpler and less interpretable process: training a compressor (or, equivalently(opens in a new window), predictor) on a very large corpus of data.1 I believe tracking the pace of progress on training better compressors is key to understanding the arc of advances in AI.
top_stories.ai_what_happened: In this post, I argue for establishing perplexity (or, equivalently, cross-entropy loss) as a metric to compare between model developers and inform shared safety standards.
ai_key_details: As a first step, I provide more transparency into pretraining progress at OpenAI.

Publishing our internal perplexity measurements took some consideration; it gives competitors a clearer picture of where we stand, but that concern is outweighed by the urgency of establishing shared(opens in a new window) safety measures across the industry.
The plot opening this blog post shows how this metric evolved for our models starting with GPT‑3.5.
GPT‑3.5, at a log-perplexity of ~0.99 on our current main evaluation dataset, was capable of fluent conversation and formed the basis for the original ChatGPT.
top_stories.ai_why_it_matters: Having experienced that allows us to extrapolate—such a sudden transformation is plausible in deep learning research too.
top_stories.ai_technical_breakdown: A simplified, but fundamentally informative, view of AI development is that first, one builds a large computer, then uses it to pretrain a model (compressor) on a large unstructured dataset, then applies a variety of techniques—like prompting, finetuning or reinforcement learning—in different contexts to elicit the latent capabilities of that model.

top_stories.ai_whats_new: Setting the new perplexity state-of-the-art on older datasets4, GPT‑2 was arguably the first model capable of consistently formulating coherent paragraphs of text.
ai_key_takeaways: We at OpenAI hope for this to be a step towards building a shared scientific basis for future pacing efforts.

Algorithmic progress can blur the distinction between training phases, but we can still separate the creation of the AI with hard-to-predict emergent capabilities (which I earlier dubbed “an alien mind”) and the subsequent targeted elicitation.

The primary way we measure progress on this key “intelligence substrate” has remained remarkably constant over the years—we have been tracking the perplexity of the models on a held-out dataset.2, 3 Perplexity measures how well a model predicts the next token on average; lower perplexity means better predictions.

top_stories.ai_overview: Today, we’re committing a portion of Anthropic’s shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new wholly owned entity with a structure that increases the stake as the company grows. Subject to stockholder approval, 5% of Anthropic’s shares will be committed today, with an additional 2% added at the board’s discretion for every 50% increase in the company’s value above a set baseline.
top_stories.ai_what_happened: As a public benefit corporation, most of our work in pursuit of our mission takes place inside the company: research relevant to AI safety and interpretability; applied biomedical research; discounts on Claude for nonprofits and scientific institutions.
ai_key_details: These activities have both a public benefit component and for-profit value, so we house them directly in the company.

The Anthropic Public Benefit Fund will have increased flexibility and scale, enabling us to pursue our mission in new ways: for example, we might explore large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations.
Anthropic has already committed $200 million to studying and addressing this issue, but given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed.

When Anthropic was founded, our co-founders pledged to donate 80% of their equity holdings, and since founding we have also operated an equity donation match program that allows employees to pledge equity which Anthropic matches.

top_stories.ai_overview: Artificial Intelligence Introducing managed cluster extensions for observability and user management in Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Slurm Keeping a shared Slurm cluster for foundation model development in sync entails keeping several separately maintained pieces of configuration matched to what’s running on the nodes. The cluster’s shape lives on multiple configuration files, its software in custom scripts, its network topology in files that must be edited as nodes change, and its users in a roster that an administrator must maintain and rerun.
top_stories.ai_what_happened: Over time these pieces drift away from what’s actually running, and nothing tells you when they do.
ai_key_details: We believe cluster configurations should be managed the way you manage the rest of your AWS infrastructure.
You declare what you want through an API or the console, AWS validates it before it’s applied, the cluster is kept in that state continuously, and you can see whether it’s working.
On Slurm 25.11 or later, partition-level topology supports tree or block topology per partition.
top_stories.ai_why_it_matters: In this post, we walk through the features we introduced in 2026 and explain why the software on running nodes needed a different mechanism.
top_stories.ai_technical_breakdown: During 2026, Amazon SageMaker HyperPod brought that approach to Slurm clusters, with API-driven Slurm configuration, AMI-based configuration, continuous provisioning, automatic topology management, and deep health checks.

dev_radar.summary: OpenAI’s layered approach to adversarial distillation combines model training, safeguards, detection, and enforcement to protect against capability extraction.
dev_radar.ai_overview: Combatting adversarial distillation How we’re addressing safety risks of distillation and lessons we’ve learned for strengthening safeguards across the industry. As frontier AI models become more capable, safeguards play an increasingly important role in how they can be used responsibly.
dev_radar.ai_what_happened: Adversarial distillation creates a path for bad actors to reproduce these capabilities without appropriate safeguards.
ai_key_details: An actor may use a frontier model’s outputs without authorization to train another model with similar capabilities, then deploy it without comparable protections.

For instance, an adversary might distill a model’s cyber capabilities and use the resulting model to help carry out cyberattacks that the original model would have refused to assist with or that its safeguards would have blocked.
We’ve strengthened our defenses against protected reasoning extraction in GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Sol.
The average attack success rate fell from 54.0% against GPT‑6 Astra with its original safeguards to 0.2% against GPT‑6.2 Astra with its updated safeguards.
dev_radar.ai_why_it_matters: Our consistent-standards policy establishes shared standards for safeguards and coordinated enforcement across providers offering our models.
dev_radar.ai_technical_breakdown: We’re sharing how OpenAI detects and disrupts adversarial distillation, how we’ve strengthened protections for our models’ protected reasoning, and what we’ve learned that can help strengthen defenses across the industry.

dev_radar.ai_whats_new: After reinforcement learning, the exact-trace student still scored higher at the largest inference budget tested on both benchmarks shown, while the summary-trained student scored higher at lower budgets.
ai_key_takeaways: Our approach to adversarial distillation combines adversarial testing, model training, classifiers, and API-level protections with investigations into coordinated attempts to extract model capabilities.
These updated safeguards align more closely with those we use for biology and cybersecurity.

We place particular emphasis on preventing attackers from extracting our models’ protected reasoning: the intermediate steps a model generates internally while working toward an answer, known as its chain-of-thought.
